statement.text: Throughout this post, by projective plane we mean the set of all lines through the origin in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Definition Say that a subset $S$ of the projective plane is octahedral if all lines in $S$ pass through the closure of two opposite faces of a regular octahedron centered at the origin. Definition Say that a subset $S$ of the projective plane is weakly octahedral if every set $S'\subseteq S$ such that $|S'|=3$ is octahedral. Conjecture Suppose that the projective plane can be partitioned into four sets, say $S_1,S_2,S_3$ and $S_4$ such that each set $S_i$ is weakly octahedral. Then each $S_i$ is octahedral.
